# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-flash_10-low-delivery-timing

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Tests **Message Delivery Timing** in isolation on `gemini-3-flash-preview` (`low` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K, per-turn step counter) across `flash_10`. Instead of injecting non-blocking peer messages into the middle of failed commands or active file-edit loops, the harness holds incoming messages up to 4 steps until a natural workflow boundary (after a passing test, git, or pull-request command, a messaging turn, or an exploration-to-editing transition; blocking waits bypass the hold immediately). Compared directly against the standardized Vertex AI `coop --git` baseline (`coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-flash-flash_10-low-stepcounter`, 6/10 overall, 3/10 clean-merge passes).

## Observations

- Clean-merge pass rate rose from 3/10 (30%) on the baseline to 4/10 (40%), and merge conflicts dropped from 3 to 2 (`typst_task/6554` reconciled into identical branches and `openai_tiktoken_task/0` merged cleanly instead of colliding).
- Headline `Passed` moved from 6/10 to 4/10 because 3 of the baseline's 6 passes (`dspy_task/8394`, `openai_tiktoken_task/0`, `typst_task/6554`) had merge conflicts and passed only via the grader's single-branch fallback when one agent implemented both features, whereas all 4 passing pairs here merged cleanly without conflict fallback.
- Total message volume dropped 28% (from 167 messages to 120, or 12.0 per pair) at slightly lower cost (`$4.04` vs. `$4.24`) with zero tool-parse or API retry errors.
